Kimberly —

Thanks for the materials and the clear checklist. Quick follow-up / clarifications from Halden legal and procurement:

1) Subprocessor detail: the manifest looks close, but we need the contractual dates for each subprocessors onboarding and whether any of them are located outside the EU (country list). Can you provide an exported subprocessor CSV with country and date columns?

2) Transfer impact: will Redwood accept the EU SCCs (2021 version) without modifying the core text? We usually expect a short Transfer Impact Addendum when onward transfers to the U.S. or other third countries occur (we can share a template).

3) KMS / encryption: we need a short KMS whitepaper and confirmation on whether customer-managed keys (for Dedicated/Private) are supported and how key access is logged.

4) Retention & deletion: procurement wants a guaranteed maximum deletion window after contract termination (we typically ask 30 days). Is Redwood able to commit to deletion within 30 days for hosted data, or do you require a longer period (our security team flagged 90 days in your draft).

5) Audit logs & access: do you provide exportable audit logs for a customer’s tenant (we want a sample log schema).

We attached a short questions PDF (haldentx_sccs_questions.pdf) with inline numbering for legal to reference when we circulate our internal redlines. If you could respond by end of Wednesday (CEST) we can target a legal handback on Thursday.

On the controller/processor mapping: our legal lead suggests clarifying the Exhibit B table so it explicitly lists which Halden services/data types are controller-side. We’ll propose edits once we see the subprocessor country list.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Data Privacy | Halden Therapeutics

Kimberly / Laura —

See Marta’s questions below. My recommended positions and action items:

- Subprocessor CSV: provide a full manifest with onboarding date and country. We already maintain that export; Kimberly please attach and call out any subprocessors that process EU personal data.
- SCCs: accept the EU SCCs (2021) but do NOT accept amendments that change the core obligations. Offer a limited Transfer Impact Addendum that documents measures and hosting commitments (scoped to Order Form regions) — this usually satisfies EU counsel.
- KMS / keys: for Dedicated/Private offer customer-managed keys (CMK) and provide the KMS whitepaper + configuration doc. For Hosted we can describe envelope encryption and key rotation; do NOT promise external KMS for hosted customers.
- Retention & deletion: push for 90 days maximum deletion window for Hosted (we need time for backups/forensic hold), but accept 30 days for Dedicated/Private with documented procedures. If Halden insists on 30d for Hosted, escalate to me — that’s a commercial concession.
- Audit logs: provide sample log schema and a standard export (90-day retention). If they need longer retention, we can offer an add-on.

Next steps (internal): Kimberly to send subprocessor CSV + KMS whitepaper + SOC2 Type II letter. Laura to prepare a short statement on encryption and log schema. I’ll draft the Transfer Impact Addendum template scoped to EU hosting regions and propose this as a middle ground.

Also flag: if Halden requests deletion proofs or on-site audit for Hosted, that will need a separate commercial addendum.

Ben Carter
